properties.map: USGS 1:62,500 topographic quadrangles: Harlem, N.Y.-N.J. (edition of 1891), Brooklyn, N.Y. (edition of 1891) — U.S. Geological Survey
properties.georeferencing: the sheets' own georeference (USGS GeoTIFF, NAD27), no further fit; offset against today's streets about 20-40 m (by eye)
properties.note: Built-up = where heavy black ink (block fronts drawn as bands at least 15 m thick, solid blocks; not road casings, thin block outlines, railways, lettering) covers more than 22 % of the ground within 80 m: about 40 % of a block's frontage built. Fully built blocks read 0.55-0.65, Central Park 0.01. Closed across streets (40 m); parts under 1.5 ha dropped, holes under 1 ha filled; piers beyond 60 m from a street of today and ink on today's railways left out. The sheets were used as georeferenced by USGS (NAD27 polyconic -> UTM 18N): against today's streets they sit within about 20-40 m (read by eye on four crops; automatic matching did not converge on these sheets), so edges are good to about one short block. Year: USGS record gives 1889 as the start of the content date range of the 1891 editions (first survey); the collar was not read. The whole of Kings County on the sheet (Brooklyn, Williamsburgh, Bushwick, and the towns of Flatbush, New Lots, Gravesend, New Utrecht, Flatlands as separate parts). West of 74 deg 00' W (the Red Hook and Bay Ridge shore) nothing was read.
